question.worked_solution:
We multiply out the parentheses and then use the identity ${cot}^{2}⁡x=\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}({cot}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cot}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}+\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int ({csc}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
